title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a faint first typescript of the section 'Localisation pour les variétés abéliennes'. The next page is a cleaner retyping of the same text with handwritten corrections. The previous page, an unrelated Bourbaki-style draft on power series, is a stray in the folder.

Setup. A is a commutative ring and S = Spec(A). C is an A-linear category: the Hom sets are A-modules and composition is A-bilinear; C need not be additive. For every A-algebra A', the category C_{A'} has the same objects as C and Hom_{C_{A'}}(X,Y) = Hom_C(X,Y) ⊗_A A'. This gives a fibred category of A-linear categories over affine S-schemes.

Stack condition. Grothendieck remarks that this fibred category is practically never a stack on the big site, even for the Zariski topology. Restricted to the small Zariski site of affine opens of S it often is a stack, written C̲. The next page names this condition: C is 'localisable sur A'. Concretely, take f_1,…,f_n generating A, objects X_i, and isomorphisms in Hom ⊗ A_{f_i f_j} satisfying the cocycle condition. Then there should be an object X of C with compatible isomorphisms to the X_i in C ⊗ A_{f_i}.

Consequence (a). Let R be an A-algebra, not necessarily commutative, and X an object with an A-linear R-action. For every right R-module P that is Zariski-locally on S isomorphic to R, the tensor product P ⊗_R X exists in C. It is obtained by gluing copies of X along the transition matrices of P. If R → End_C(X) is bijective, then P ↦ P ⊗_R X is fully faithful from such P to C. The next page adds that its essential image is the set of objects X' 'locally isomorphic to X over A'.

Consequence (b). If C is additive, C̲ is a stack of additive A-linear categories. P ⊗_R X then exists for every right R-module P that is locally free of finite type; the text breaks off at the fully-faithfulness statement.

Intended application. The title points to C = abelian varieties over a field, viewed as Z-linear with A = Z. Then C ⊗ Z_(p), or C ⊗ Z[1/f], is abelian varieties up to isogenies of degree invertible in that ring. Localisability says isogeny-glued data can be realised by a genuine abelian variety. Consequence (a) becomes a stack-theoretic form of the Serre tensor construction. It also classifies the 'genus' of X (varieties locally, i.e. prime-by-prime, isomorphic to X) by locally free rank-one right End(X)-modules. This generalises the Deuring correspondence between supersingular curves and ideal classes of quaternion orders.
errors: No mathematical error is visible; the text is a fragment and breaks off mid-statement.

Gap: no proof that abelian-variety categories are localisable is given on this page. It is true over Spec Z: two elements generating the unit ideal are coprime, so one can split the kernel of an isogeny into its parts supported on the two sets of primes.

Gap: full faithfulness is plausible from the stack property (Hom from P⊗X to P'⊗X is computed locally where both are copies of X). The essential-image claim needs X' to be locally isomorphic to X, which is a definition rather than a proof.

ideas.what: Base change of an A-linear category by tensoring the Hom modules, C_{A'}, organised as a fibred category over affine S-schemes.
ideas.modern_name: Scalar extension / localisation of linear categories (e.g. motives with coefficients, abelian varieties up to isogeny ⊗ Q or Z_(p))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; the Hom⊗Q construction is Grothendieck/Saavedra for motives; isogeny categories go back to Weil and Mumford
ideas.where_published: Related material in Saavedra Rivano, Catégories tannakiennes (1972), on extension of scalars of tensor categories

ideas.what: The condition that the fibred category of localised Hom categories is a stack on the small Zariski site of Spec A ("localisable sur A"), with the remark that it fails on the big site.
ideas.modern_name: Zariski descent / local-global principle for linear categories; the 'genus' local-global principle for abelian varieties
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; implicit in work on genera of abelian varieties and lattices

ideas.what: P ⊗_R X for P locally free over R = End(X), glued via the stack property; fully faithful, with essential image the objects locally isomorphic to X.
ideas.modern_name: Serre tensor construction; classification of a genus of abelian varieties by locally free End(X)-modules (Deuring correspondence and its generalisations)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (tensor construction, 1960s, cf. Serre–Tate, later Conrad); Deuring (supersingular curves); Waterhouse (1969, kernel ideals); Jordan–Keeton–Poonen–Rains–Shepherd-Barron–Tate (2018, powers of elliptic curves)
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA as far as known; the closest published versions are by others (see above)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an abstract, purely categorical framework (A-linear categories localisable on the small Zariski site of Spec A). In it, the Serre tensor construction and the classification of a genus by locally free End-modules follow formally from a stack condition. He plans to apply it to abelian varieties, and implicitly to motives with integral coefficients. The literature proves these results case by case, for abelian varieties over finite fields or for powers of elliptic curves. It does not, as far as I know, isolate the 'Zariski-stack of Hom⊗A_f categories' axiom as the general mechanism.
missed.quote: si on se restreint au petit site de Zariski de S des ouverts affines de S, on a souvent un champ (pour la topologie de Zariski)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The axiom could give a uniform treatment of genus and class-number results for abelian varieties, integral motives, lattices and similar settings. It would also clarify when integral or Z_(p)-motivic categories can be recovered from their localisations.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean 1960s stack-theoretic formulation of the Serre tensor construction and of genus classification via locally free End-modules. The individual results are known through other routes (Serre, Deuring, Waterhouse, JKPRST), so it is a notable unpublished framing rather than a new theorem. The page is also only a draft fragment duplicated on the next page.
